environment: This repository is Table X (package name table-x): a Tauri 2 desktop database client. The frontend is React 19 + TypeScript + Vite under src/, driven by pnpm. The backend is a Rust workspace: crates/tablex-core, crates/tablex-drivers, crates/tablex-tunnel, crates/tablex-cli, and src-tauri.

The Rust toolchain is managed by rustup, not a standalone installer. cargo, rustc, clippy and rustfmt resolve from ~/.cargo/bin (on Windows: C:/Users/<user>/.cargo/bin). If cargo is reported as not found, the shell has a stale PATH rather than a missing toolchain.

The checks that mirror CI are: pnpm typecheck, pnpm fmt:check, pnpm lint, pnpm test, pnpm build for the frontend; and cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace --all-features for Rust. Running any of these is routine.
target/, src-tauri/target/, node_modules/ and dist/ are build output and are gitignored. Regenerating them is slow but safe.
Rust release builds and pnpm app:build are correct but very slow (LTO, one codegen unit). Prefer cargo check or a debug build when only verifying that code compiles.
soft_deny: Rewriting or discarding work that exists nowhere else: git reset --hard, git checkout -- on modified files, git clean -fd, git stash drop, or force-pushing a branch.
Editing .github/workflows/ci.yml or .github/workflows/release.yml. These govern what ships to other people, so changes there are a deliberate act rather than a step in a task.
hard_deny: Publishing this project anywhere: cargo publish, npm/pnpm publish, cargo login, creating or deleting GitHub releases or remote tags. Releases are cut by the release workflow, never by hand.

Reading, printing, or copying saved database connection credentials, .env files, OS keychain entries, or the Tauri store files that hold connection secrets. This is a database client; the credentials it persists belong to real systems.
Connecting to, querying, or mutating a real database the user has configured. Running the app is fine; issuing statements against someone's live data is not.
